Chapter 9: Giving Back—Becoming Mentors and Leaders
As time goes by, something amazing happens. Those students who once leaned so heavily on mentors and their community? They find themselves stepping into entirely new roles.
The wisdom they’ve picked up along the way—like the strength in being vulnerable, the grit that comes with resilience, and the comfort of community—suddenly feels like something precious. And now, they’re ready to pass it on.
You know, some of them choose to return to the places they grew up. Maybe they volunteer at a local school or spend afternoons at the community center. When they look around, they see younger versions of themselves—kids who might be quiet, a little guarded, maybe even unsure where they belong. And with patience and genuine empathy, they step in to guide, to listen, and to support—just like someone once did for them.
Others give back in different ways, woven right into their everyday work. Picture a nurse who calms a scared patient, because she remembers what it’s like to be afraid and uncertain. Or a teacher who makes sure every student feels noticed, creating a classroom where no one’s invisible. Or a social worker who stands up for families in crisis, knowing exactly how it feels to be overlooked.
Here’s something to remember: giving back doesn’t have to be a big, dramatic gesture. Most of the time, it’s much simpler. Maybe it’s just listening—really listening—to a friend. Or offering a few words of encouragement. Or sharing a story that helps someone realize they’re not alone. Each small act starts a ripple, inspiring kindness in ways you might never see.
For a lot of people, mentoring is a way to say thank you—to honor those who once helped them. But it’s also about claiming a sense of agency. It’s refusing to let cycles of hardship or silence just keep going. By stepping up as leaders, these young adults become real agents of change, shaping their communities from the inside out.
When you look back, you realize the journey isn’t just about growing as a person. It’s really about collective healing. Most of us don’t fully grasp how much a single act of kindness can change someone’s life—until we see it come full circle, reflected in the lives of others.
